title: Rank-zero and rank-one Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer theory, Part II: Eisenstein converses and twist proportions
summary: This Part II of RankZeroOneBSD supplies the good odd Eisenstein-prime converse in Selmer coranks zero and one, its finite-Selmer form, and positive proportions of low-rank quadratic twists on the precisely admissible local family. The proof combines complementary twists, rational augmentation control and the parent’s Heegner index-square equality. CM rank-zero converses and Skinner’s irreducible branch retain their existing owners. All six layers are planned; the shared Cassels–Tate supplier endpoint is an explicit frontier, and no implementation is claimed.
readme: The full specification is research/blueprint/readmes/RankZeroOneBSDPartII.md. This Part II of RankZeroOneBSD supplies the good odd Eisenstein-prime converse in Selmer coranks zero and one, its finite-Selmer form, and positive proportions of low-rank quadratic twists on the precisely admissible local family. The proof combines complementary twists, rational augmentation control and the parent’s Heegner index-square equality. CM rank-zero converses and Skinner’s irreducible branch retain their existing owners. All six layers are planned; the shared Cassels–Tate supplier endpoint is an explicit frontier, and no implementation is claimed. The exact good-reduction and local-character conditions persist in each twist application. The endpoint is equality of analytic and arithmetic ranks and full Sha finiteness, without a BSD leading-term identity. The CM and Skinner routes are imports from CMRankZeroConverse and RankOneConverse, with routing reconciliation recorded in the packet.

stages.title: Fixed isogenies and low-dimensional Selmer groups
stages.description: Pin the actual isogeny kernel and the good odd-prime local exclusion. Import ordinarity and torsion vanishing, the canonical Selmer carriers and modular parity. Compare a zero- or one-dimensional finite Selmer group with p∞ corank using the shared Cassels–Tate pairing modulo its divisible kernels.

stages.title: Complementary twists and Heegner fields
stages.description: Use the imported ordinary modular parity and both twist-nonvanishing branches to choose imaginary quadratic K with all level primes and p split, odd D<−4 and analytic twist rank1−r. Apply the forward theorem to the twist and odd-primary quadratic descent to establish corank Sel(E/K)=1 before using a main conjecture.

stages.title: Augmentation control and the bottom Heegner point
stages.description: Prove rational ordinary control at P₀=(γ−1), with finite local errors and the compact specialization kernel explicit. Under corank1 show v_P₀(char X_tors)=0. Apply the parent’s CGLS Heegner index-square equality in Λ[1/p], identify the precise stabilized bottom-class factor and deduce a non-torsion classical Heegner point and a simple zero over K.

stages.title: The Eisenstein-prime converses
stages.description: For r=0,1 prove corank Sel_(p∞)(E/ℚ)=r implies analyticRank(E)=r by subtracting the complementary twist’s order from the simple base-change order. Import the shared p-converse proposition. Deduce equality of Mordell–Weil rank and full Sha finiteness from the forward theorem, then the finite-Selmer version without assuming Sha finite.

stages.title: Admissible quadratic twists and positive proportions
stages.description: Define the local 3 admissible subset of the existing squareclass-height twist family. Under existence of a good-at-3 twist, choose zero and odd Selmer-ratio strata while holding an admissible3-adic class fixed. Import BKLOS’s restricted-family 1/2 and 5/6 Selmer bounds, apply the finite-Selmer converse, and state positive absolute lower proportions with all denominator factors.

stages.title: Concrete models and scope diagnostics
stages.description: Specify nineteenA3 on Mathlib’s Weierstrass carrier with invariant, twist-normalization and rational 3-torsion tests. Compute its local admissible density 3/8 and the resulting ceiling on this method’s conversion set. Exhibit y²+xy+3y=x³ with v₃(j)=−3, proving that a rational 3-isogeny does not guarantee any good-at-3 quadratic twist.
